authority_citations: REQ-SAG-0009 v2 (locked, prohibition) statement: No low-level sc-agent crate (types, config, secrets, log, http, decision schema, decision backends, runner) must depend on tokio with its default features.
REQ-SAG-0009 v2 quote: A program that does not use tokio MUST be able to use every low-level crate.
REQ-SAG-0009 v2 scope: adds or changes dependencies of a low-level sc-agent crate.
phase-a-intent v1: the decide CLI design beyond what the low-level libraries must support is out of scope.

item.text: `cargo tree -p sc-decision-runner` lists no tokio crate with default features.
item.title: Verify runner dependency tree

cases.rationale: Approved pass fixture of REQ-SAG-0009. The item concerns the runner's dependency tree (in scope) and states the prohibition's specific content (no tokio with default features), so addressed is yes and nothing conflicts.

item.text: sc-agent-http adds reqwest with its default tokio runtime as a required dependency.
item.title: HTTP client dependency

cases.rationale: Approved fail fixture of REQ-SAG-0009. sc-agent-http is a listed low-level crate; a required dependency on reqwest's default tokio runtime makes it depend on tokio with default features, which the statement prohibits. The item does not carry the prohibition.

item.text: sc-agent-http adds ureq, a blocking HTTP client with no async runtime, as its only HTTP dependency. No low-level crate depends on tokio, so a program that does not use tokio can use sc-agent-http.
item.title: Blocking HTTP client for sc-agent-http

cases.rationale: Adds a dependency to a listed low-level crate (in scope), explicitly states that no low-level crate depends on tokio, and nothing in it adds tokio. Satisfies REQ-SAG-0009.

item.text: sc-agent-types adds serde (with the derive feature) and serde_json as dependencies so the TypeSafe request and response types can be serialized.
item.title: Serialization for sc-agent-types

cases.rationale: Adds dependencies to a listed low-level crate, which is exactly the anchor's scope, so relevant is yes. The item says nothing about tokio, so addressed is no; serde and serde_json add no tokio, and silence is not a conflict. A prohibition is satisfied by refraining.

item.text: Decide how sc-decision-runner executes a batch of decision requests in parallel, comparing a thread pool with an async runtime, and record the choice in an ADR before implementation.
item.title: Choose the runner's parallel execution mechanism

cases.rationale: Plans the runner's execution mechanism, a direct prerequisite of the runner's runtime dependencies, so relevant is yes. It mentions an async runtime but neither states the no-tokio-default-features constraint (addressed no) nor commits to tokio with default features (contradicted no); an open choice is not a conflict with the prohibition.

item.text: sc-decision-runner runs decision batches in parallel on a tokio runtime, adding `tokio = { version = "1", features = ["full"] }` as a required dependency.
item.title: Parallel batches in the runner

cases.rationale: The runner is a listed low-level crate; a required tokio dependency with default (and all) features is what REQ-SAG-0009 prohibits, and a program without tokio could not use the runner.

item.text: In sc-decision-schema, rename the `DecisionOutcome::Reject` variant to `Declined` and update its doc comments and tests.
item.title: Rename a decision outcome variant

cases.rationale: A rename inside a low-level crate that neither adds nor changes any dependency is outside the anchor's scope (adds or changes dependencies) and does not touch tokio.

item.text: sc-decision-runner adds an optional `tokio` cargo feature, off by default, that enables `tokio = { version = "1", default-features = false, features = ["rt"] }`. Without the feature the runner has no tokio dependency, and tokio's default features are never enabled.
item.title: Optional tokio integration for the runner

cases.rationale: The statement prohibits depending on tokio with its default features; this item depends on tokio only optionally and with default-features = false, and explicitly states that tokio's default features are never enabled, so it carries the prohibition and does not conflict. Programs without tokio can use the runner (quote).

item.text: The decide command-line binary crate adds tokio with its default features to drive its async main loop.
item.title: Async main for the decide CLI

cases.rationale: REQ-SAG-0009 governs only the enumerated low-level crates (types, config, secrets, log, http, decision schema, decision backends, runner); the decide CLI binary is not one of them and its design is out of scope per INTENT. Its tokio dependency is therefore outside the anchor, not a conflict.
